passage:
A city tested special paint on roads and rooftops to reflect more sunlight. The painted areas stayed cooler than dark surfaces nearby.
Residents liked the idea, but some worried about cost and how long the paint would last.
Students measured temperatures for a science project. They found real differences, especially in open areas without trees.
Their teacher said cooling a city requires many methods: shade, materials, water, buildings, and behavior.
The paint was useful, but not enough alone.
Heat is a design problem as well as a weather problem. The color of a surface can affect how a whole street feels.
